subject: Acme AI bake-off: discovery recap & proposed evaluation plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Wong <sarah.wong@acme.ai>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Acme AI bake-off: discovery recap & proposed evaluation plan

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and a proposed next steps list so we can get the bake-off scheduled. High-level summary first, then specifics.

Pain points you shared
- Production latency spikes on our in-house vLLM endpoints during peak loads (especially long-context chat flows).
- Cost per query is higher than expected; need clear unit economics for 1M requests/month.
- Occasional quality regressions after model updates — lack a repeatable eval pipeline tied to production prompts.

Current stack and constraints
- Serving: in-house vLLM for most ops; experimenting with TGI on k8s for some endpoints.
- Data: customer prompt history stored in US-region S3 buckets; PII redaction happens upstream.
- Security: must remain within US region for PII workloads; SOC2 compliance is important for legal.

Success criteria (as discussed)
- Latency: p95 inference latency <= 250ms on typical 512-token prompts (target for human-facing chat flows).
- Throughput: sustain 80 qps (concurrent small requests) for batch workflows.
- Cost: per-1k-token unit cost (tokens normalized) that shows >=20% reduction vs current vLLM infra.
- Quality: >=95% parity on your internal prompt set (we'll use your golden prompts for regression checks); no user-facing regressions during the POC.
- Operational: ability to pin model versions and automatic fallback to lower-capacity region without cold starts.

Proposed bake-off setup (what we'll run)
1) Benchmarks we will run (we'll provide a template):
   - Latency (p50/p95/p99) for 256/512/2k token sequences.
   - Throughput: sustained qps tests at 20/50/80 qps.
   - Cost estimate: tokens/sec and cost per 1k tokens at target throughput.
   - Quality/regression: run your golden prompt set against candidate model variants and baseline vLLM/TGI/cloud endpoints (we'll compare exact-match/F1 where applicable and manual spot checks).
2) Data & access needed:
   - A redacted sample of ~2000 golden prompts (we discussed PII removal) via S3 link.
   - Network access for load tests (we can run from Redwood hosted agents or in your VPC for private evaluation).
3) Duration & acceptance:
   - 2-week bake-off window (config + warm-up week + measurement week).
   - Acceptance: meet latency + throughput targets and evidence of >=20% cost improvement or equivalent operational benefits.

Attachments + links
- Attached: acme-bakeoff-benchmark-template.xlsx (benchmark metrics + sample scripts).
- Redwood SOC2 summary (attached) and a Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake/acme-bakeoff-template

Next steps
- Please confirm the acceptance criteria above and tell us whether you prefer Redwood-hosted test agents or running the tests from your VPC.
- Share the redacted golden prompt set (or a link) and a preferred kickoff date.
- I'll schedule a 30-min technical kickoff with Rishi if you want to review the test harness and network setup.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this running.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0124
[Attachment: acme-bakeoff-benchmark-template.xlsx]

From: Sarah Wong <sarah.wong@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme AI bake-off: discovery recap & proposed evaluation plan

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful and aligns with what we talked about. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Acceptance criteria: the latency p95 target should be <= 200ms for our 512-token median case to be considered a clear win. We can be flexible on p99 but p95 is critical.
- Quality: for the golden set, we expect automated metrics + a quick 10-user manual review sample. If the automated metrics are borderline, the manual pass/fail will be decisive.
- Data residency: all PII test payloads must remain in US-only regions; we will provide an S3 link with proper IAM roles.

We prefer Redwood-hosted test agents initially (simpler), but we may ask to run the final validation from our VPC.
\We're aiming to kick off the week of Sep 7 — does that work for you? Also can you share the SOC2 summary and any standard NDA/POC template we should review?

Appreciate it,
Sarah
Sr Product Manager, Acme AI
sarah.wong@acme.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Wong <sarah.wong@acme.ai>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme AI bake-off: discovery recap & proposed evaluation plan

Thanks Sarah — great notes. Quick replies inline: 

- Latency: we can prioritize p95 <= 200ms for 512-token profiles; we'll tune batching and KV cache to hit that target during the measurement window.
- Quality checks: we'll run automated metrics (exact-match / BLEU / chosen metrics) + set up a 10-person manual review panel for final assessment; we'll include a pass/fail rubric in the template.
- SOC2 & NDA: attaching the SOC2 summary (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf). I'll also send our standard POC MSA / NDA for quick review (link below).
\Bake-off plan (details):
- Week 0 (prep): exchange golden prompts (redacted), confirm test harness (we'll provide runner scripts), and baseline current vLLM/TGI/cloud numbers.
- Week 1 (warmup): deploy candidate config(s) and run steady-state warmup.
- Week 2 (measure): run five measurement windows (3x short-run latency, 2x longer throughput runs) and collate results.
\Benchmarks and comparators: we'll benchmark against:
- Your current vLLM baseline (we'll request a short baseline run from you).
- TGI on your k8s baseline (if available).
- Cloud endpoints (we'll use public cloud endpoints as a third comparator).
\Action items:
- Sarah: confirm Sep 7 kickoff week (you said week of Sep 7)
- Acme: provide S3 link with sample prompts and IAM role by Sep 3
- Redwood (Rishi): outline required network access and test runner options — can you provide a short checklist?
\Doc links: SOC2 summary attached; POC template: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ACME-2026-INV-43
\I'll tentatively book kickoff for Sep 8 at 10am PT; if that doesn't work, let me know.
\Best,
Marissa
[Attachment: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sarah Wong <sarah.wong@acme.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme AI bake-off: discovery recap & proposed evaluation plan
\Hi all — adding a few technical clarifications so the benchmark runs are deterministic and comparable: \n
1) Request patterns: please confirm distribution of prompt lengths (we saw ~60% short <128 tokens, 30% 128-512, 10% >512). If your mix is different we'll adapt the test harness.
2) KV cache / prefix caching: to hit the p95 target we'll need to know whether persistent KV caching is acceptable in your environment; otherwise cold-starts will skew p99/p95.
3) Model variants: which model families do you want to include? We can test equivalently-sized Llama-family models, quantized variants (4-bit), and a cloud endpoint baseline.
4) TLS/Network: For Redwood-hosted agents we'll need to whitelist agent IPs; for VPC runs we'll provide an AMI with our runner. Also confirm whether S3 signed URLs are acceptable for test payloads.
\Deliverables from Redwood for the kickoff:
- Test runner (Docker image) and runbook.
- Baseline scripts and expected CSV output format.
- A short checklist of whitelist / IAM steps (I'll post that in the shared Drive link).
\I can run through the checklist in the kickoff call.
\Thanks,
Rishi
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
